question: What's the best solar generator for power outages?
query: best solar generators portable power stations for home power outages 2026 reviews capacity expandable solar charging

judge.why: The answer recommends EcoFlow, Anker and Jackery units, none of which we sell, and it cites Anker, Home Depot, OutdoorGearLab and Consumer Reports instead of dealectric.com.

replays.text:
Based on the 9 reviews you collected, **the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the best overall solar generator for home power outages.**

It's the strongest choice if you want to keep essential appliances running, recharge with solar during an extended outage, and expand your backup system over time.

## 🏆 Best overall: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3

<AsyncImageGroup query={["EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 portable power station front view","EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 with extra battery and solar panels home backup setup"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="bento"/>

**Why it's the best:**
- **4,096 Wh capacity** — substantial energy storage for essential household appliances.
- **4,000 W output** — handles more demanding appliances than smaller portable power stations.
- **Expandable up to 48 kWh** — add batteries as your backup needs grow.
- **Up to 2,600 W solar input** — supports substantial solar recharging during prolonged outages.
- **120/240V capability** — particularly useful for home backup applications.
- **Transfer switch compatibility** — can connect to essential home circuits with the appropriate equipment.

**What the reviewers say:** OutdoorGearLab highlights its power and battery expansion potential, while PowerOutage.us and The Solar Lab independently recommend it for home backup.

Sources: [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) · [PowerOutage.us](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators) · [The Solar Lab](https://www.thesolarlab.com/best-of/home-backup-power-stations)

    </box>
  </row>

    <box flex="1">

      [Anker SOLIX F3800](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
    </box>
  </row>

    <box flex="1">

    </box>
  </row>

      [Pecron F5000LFP](https://www.solargenadvisor.com/best-solar-generators/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## Which size do you actually need?

| Your backup goal | My recommendation |
|---|---|
| Phones, Wi-Fi, lights, laptops | 1–2 kWh |
| Refrigerator, lights, electronics | 2–4 kWh |
| Multiple appliances for longer outages | 4–8 kWh+ |
| Essential home circuits, extended outages | Expandable system, such as DELTA Pro 3 |

## One important caveat

Consumer Reports emphasizes that portable battery generators are best for outages lasting **hours rather than days** unless you carefully manage power consumption and have sufficient solar recharging.

A refrigerator, for example, consumes energy continuously over time, so battery capacity (Wh or kWh) is just as important as inverter output (W).

Also, powering an entire home's 240V circuits is different from plugging individual appliances into a power station. Proper transfer equipment and installation may be required.

[Consumer Reports: Portable Power Station Reviews](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/)

---

### My bottom line

If I were choosing one specifically for **home power outages with solar recharging and future expandability**, I'd choose the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**.

The next most useful step is sizing it to your actual household needs. I can calculate how many hours it would run your refrigerator, Wi-Fi, lights, and other essential appliances using realistic power consumption estimates.
